instructions: On Sunday, or up to 3 days ahead: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a 12-cup muffin tin with paper liners. Melt the 1/2 cup butter in a large bowl in the microwave, about 1 minute.
In a second large bowl, whisk the 2 1/2 cups flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp baking soda and 1/2 tsp salt.
Whisk the 3/4 cup sugar and 1/2 cup brown sugar into the melted butter until it's smooth. Whisk in the 1 cup milk, 2 eggs and 2 tsp vanilla.
Peel and core the apples, then chop them small, about 1/4 inch. That should be about 2 cups.
Pour the wet mix into the flour bowl and fold until there's no dry flour left. A few lumps are fine. Fold in the apples and 2 tsp cinnamon. Stop as soon as they're mixed in.
Divide the batter among the 12 cups and fill each to the top.
Bake at 400°F for 5 minutes, then turn the oven down to 350°F and bake for 16 to 17 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Keep the oven door shut when you turn it down.
Cool the muffins in the pan for 5 minutes, then move them to a rack to cool completely. This makes 12 muffins.
Fridge: keep them in a sealed container with a paper towel on top for up to 5 days.
Freezer: spread the cooled muffins in a single layer on a tray and freeze for about 2 hours, until solid. Transfer them into a freezer bag. They keep for up to 3 months.
In the morning, warm a fridge muffin in the microwave for 20 to 30 seconds. For a frozen one, microwave it for 45 to 60 seconds, until warm in the middle.
advance_prep_notes: Bake the whole batch on Sunday, or up to 3 days ahead, and keep the muffins in the fridge or freezer.
method_notes: Wholefully's version is the lead: a plain muffin with the apple chopped small, and a hot start (5 minutes at 400°F, then 350°F) that gives tall tops. Love and Lemons also hot-starts at 400°F and uses the same 2 cups of apple, but it leans on almond flour, so none of it was used here. Wholefully shows 18 muffins on the card but bakes in a 12-cup tin, so this is written as 12 tall ones. Both sources freeze the muffins for up to 3 months.
